restrictions: 2026-11-14, THE UI IS NOW C++ WITH GTKMM BUILT WITH CMAKE (ADR 0006): this verdict was written for the C UI built with Meson (executable 733389c1). Every restriction below that speaks of 'the current build', main.c, gtk_*_ C calls, the meson options or 54,016 bytes describes THAT C build and stays as history. The current build is executable 44cba2ef (167,192 bytes: gtkmm-3.0 3.24.9 on GTK 3.24.41, UI compiled as C++11, backend libloomora compiled with -std=c++11, both checked in compile_commands.json, gcc 13.3.0, Release, 0 warnings), built by 'python tools/build.py linux modern'. VERIFIED ON IT (2026-11-14): 15 of 15 vectors of tools/run_vectors.py, run through the Windows launcher and inside WSL, and also with the floor build (a93d4bf5), the GTK 4 build (0ce25e43) and the static-C++-runtime build (4d9be3da) through --exe; tools/check_probe.py OK on the probe lines; 20 probe runs (10x --probe, 10x --probe-input Marie: exit 0, empty stderr, no leftover process, display_ms 90 to 152, median 101.5, peak_rss_kb 45820 to 46600, against 91 to 239 and 37716 to 38336 for the C build); a window without --probe for 6 s on the X11 backend (still running, empty stderr, exit 0 when closed) and on the Wayland backend (still running, empty stderr, SIGTERM); typing Marie with XTEST key events (Ctrl+A then M a r i e: 'Bonjour Marie', 3 ms from the last key to the changed pixels); 1,100 typed characters cut at 1,000 (the greeting ends with the token 0200); a 250-character greeting wrapped and scrolled with a visible scrollbar; the end-of-life banner with a faked kernel and its close button; glyph captures looked at one by one: Latin accents and Latin Extended, the euro sign, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji (ZWJ family, flag, skin tone), Hebrew and Arabic (right to left), combining marks, symbols; ctest 2 of 2 (the UI built in the same CMake tree) and tools/check_std.py 0 failures. STORED (new proof of the new toolkit, with sha256, in validation/evidence/gtkmm-cmake/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/): the screenshots, three probe lines, the gui run records, the 20-run measurement, and the before/after build measurements. NOT stored, results above only: the 15 vectors and their probe lines, check_probe on every line of the series, ctest, check_std, the runs of the floor and static builds beyond one screenshot and one start each, the GTK 4 vectors (re-runs, CLAUDE.md).

NOT RE-RUN ON THE C++ BUILD: the three forced GTK themes (Adwaita:dark, HighContrast, HighContrastInverse) and the contrast ratios of the C trial (the default theme gave 11.61 again), the cross-check of peak_rss_kb with os.wait4 beyond what probe-series.py records (ru_maxrss 46016 to 46684 kB, 84 to 368 kB above the probe's VmHWM), memory with a long greeting, a real person typing, IME, clipboard, dead keys. The restrictions NO PERSON, BACKENDS, END-OF-LIFE BANNER IS A SIMULATION, SCREENSHOTS and ENVIRONMENT below apply to the new build unchanged (the faked kernel 2.6.32 shim, client-area captures, one WSL2 environment).

SHARED X SERVER, 2026-11-14: another change (the Linux Legacy UI, also titled 'Loomora') was run against the same WSLg X server at the same time. The window drivers of the C trial look a window up by its title and the first screenshots of this trial captured the other program's window (recognised by its look and discarded). gtkmm-gui-driver.py and gtkmm-glyphs-shoot.py (derived from the stored drivers, which are untouched) look the window up by its title AND the _NET_WM_PID of the process they started, ignore X errors of vanishing windows, and each run waited for a moment without any other Loomora program before it started; the XTEST keys of two such drivers could still reach the other's window, so every typed run was checked on its screenshot (the stored ones show the typed text in the right window). The new drivers also add the vectors euro, greek and cyrillic.

GTKMM AND THE GTK 3.10 FLOOR: the floor build (LOOMORA_GTK_FLOOR=ON, ADR 0006) compiles the 3.10 path only (executable a93d4bf5 imports Gtk::Misc::set_alignment, not Gtk::Label::set_xalign or Gtk::ScrolledWindow::set_overlay_scrolling) and rejects any GTK or GDK C symbol newer than 3.10, but a gtkmm METHOD is not marked by GTK: label.set_xalign(0) compiles in the floor build. That the gtkmm calls of the 3.10 path exist in gtkmm 3.10 (the version of Ubuntu 14.04) is a hand check against the GTK versions of the functions they wrap (the table of ADR 0006), not a compiler check, and no gtkmm 3.10 header or system was available: NOT verified. Whether the glibmm and libsigc++ of such a system accept the C++11 lambdas and -std=c++11 of this UI was not tried. The executable links libgtkmm-3.0.so.1 (GTK 3.24 symbols), so it runs only with the gtkmm of its build.

NEW RUN-TIME DEPENDENCIES: the C++ build needs libgtkmm-3.0, libatkmm-1.6, libgiomm-2.4, libpangomm-1.4, libglibmm-2.4 and libsigc-2.0 in addition to GTK (9 direct DT_NEEDED entries, 79 libraries resolved by ldd against 7 and 71 for the C build); highest symbol versions GLIBC_2.34, GLIBCXX_3.4.21, CXXABI_1.3, the same as the C build (std::strtoll and std::sscanf were replaced because g++ binds them to GLIBC_2.38 symbols). The static-C++-runtime option (LOOMORA_STATIC_CXX_RUNTIME) builds and passes 15 of 15 vectors and starts a window, but it no longer serves its purpose with gtkmm (libglibmm etc. still need libstdc++.so.6, so the process holds two copies of the runtime): 1,998,448 bytes, GLIBC_2.38. A display that cannot be opened ends with status 1 and GTK's own message (checked with DISPLAY unset and GDK_BACKEND=x11), not with 'loomora: cannot open the display'. The GTK 4 build (gtkmm-4.0 4.10.0, C++17) has no verdict: screenshots, the vectors and the start are the verification of ADR 0006, not a trial.

[C UI, until 2026-11-14] VERIFIED ON THE BUILD OF 2026-11-13 (executable 733389c1, 54,016 bytes, default meson options, GTK 3.24.41 headers; 2026-11-13): 20 probe runs (10x --probe, 10x --probe-input Marie: exit 0, empty stderr, no leftover process, display_ms 91 to 239, peak_rss_kb 37716 to 38336), 15 of 15 vectors of tools/run_vectors.py, a window without --probe for 6 s with empty stderr (X11 and Wayland backends), typing "Marie" with real XTEST key events ("Bonjour Marie" in the default, Adwaita:dark, HighContrast and HighContrastInverse themes), 1,100 typed characters cut at 1,000, a long greeting with a visible scrollbar scrolled with the mouse wheel, the end-of-life banner with a faked kernel, 13 glyph captures with the Noto fonts. Only the files that prove something new are stored in the evidence with their sha256 (CLAUDE.md): the visible scrollbar, the 1,100-character limit, the Wayland start, the end-of-life banner and 3 of the glyph captures; the 20 probe runs, the 15 vectors, the X11 start, the four themes typed with XTEST and the other glyph captures of that list are re-runs of behaviour the first trial already evidenced, their results are stated here but their files are NOT stored. The evidence files of the executables 5bd33f1d, f83a1a13 and 24b62caf are kept as history; none of them is evidence for the current build.

NO PERSON: nobody typed in the window. The keys, wheel and click are synthetic XTEST events injected into the X11 session of WSLg (XWayland) by a script; they reach the focused window through the X server like keyboard events, but a real keyboard, key repeat, input methods and IME, dead keys, copy and paste, drag and drop, and mouse selection were not tried. Only ASCII characters were typed; the non-ASCII texts (accents, CJK, emoji, Hebrew, Arabic) reached the field through --probe-input, not through the keyboard. The 3 ms from the last key to the changed greeting pixels is an upper bound taken with polled captures of the X11 window, not the delay as seen by an eye on a screen.

BACKENDS: the typing, scrolling and banner runs used GDK_BACKEND=x11 (XWayland). The default backend of this system is Wayland, on which the application was only run for 6 s without --probe (empty stderr, no screenshot, no input, no clean close: ended with SIGTERM); the 20 probe runs and the 15 vectors use the default Wayland backend. No screenshot shows the process of the timing runs. 'displayed' in the probe record is the application's own first draw callback; that the compositor put the pixels on a screen was not independently checked.

END-OF-LIFE BANNER IS A SIMULATION: uname(2) was faked to 2.6.32 with an LD_PRELOAD shim (fake-uname.c, built in a scratch directory). The banner (FR-013, ui-contract item 3) was displayed, its text read in the screenshot, and closed with a click on its button, and the probe line reported eol_warning_shown true; but the WSL2 kernel (6.18.58.1) is not end of life and the banner has not been shown on a REAL old kernel or an end-of-life distribution. With the banner the window opens 480x430 instead of 480x240 and does not shrink when the banner is closed (already noted in ADR 0005, not changed).

THEMES: dark and high contrast were forced with GTK_THEME (Adwaita:dark, HighContrast, HighContrastInverse), not through the desktop settings (gsettings color-scheme, the accessibility high-contrast switch, the Ubuntu Yaru theme); the image has no full desktop session. Contrast ratios measured on the captured pixels of the greeting: 11.61, 10.56, 13.88 and 11.88, all above 4.5:1. The HighContrast theme rendered by GTK 3.24 looks almost like the default theme (near-white background, near-black text), so it is not evidence for the real high-contrast mode of a desktop.

SCREENSHOTS are captures of the window client area (Gdk pixbuf of the X11 window, 480x240, 480x430 with the banner): no title bar, no decoration, no desktop, no screen recording. Glyph rendering was looked at by the author of the trial for accents, Latin Extended, CJK, emoji (ZWJ family, flag, skin tone), Hebrew and Arabic (right-to-left order correct in the label, field right-aligned), combining marks (Latin, Thai, Devanagari) and symbols with ONE font set (Noto Sans, Noto Sans CJK, Noto Color Emoji, DejaVu) and ONE theme engine; the box-drawing string is drawn as a single small bracket-like glyph and was not compared with a reference. Other font sets, other desktops, real GPUs and a person reading the screen were not checked. Missing fonts are an environment limit, not a UI defect: with only DejaVu, Ubuntu and MathJax fonts CJK, Thai, Devanagari and most emoji code points were drawn as hexadecimal boxes in both the field and the label (history, executable 5bd33f1d: glyphs-dejavu-only-*.png); the packages that fix it on Ubuntu are fonts-noto-cjk, fonts-noto-color-emoji and fonts-noto-core.

GTK VERSIONS: only GTK 3.24.41 was run. The current build takes the 3.16 path (gtk_label_set_xalign and gtk_scrolled_window_set_overlay_scrolling(FALSE), macros LOOMORA_GTK_HAS_*) which no GTK older than 3.16 would have; the 3.10 path (gtk_misc_set_alignment, no overlay call) exists only in the floor build (-Dgtk_floor=true, ADR 0005), which the policy work compiled without warnings and ran for the probe, the vectors and a 4-second window on GTK 3.24, but this trial did NOT re-run it. A real GTK 3.10, versions between 3.10 and 3.24, GTK 4 (-Dgtk_api=4: no verdict and no deliverable record, built and checked only by the policy work) and the floor build's scrollbar on a runtime with overlay scrolling are not verified here.

ENVIRONMENT: one environment only, Ubuntu 24.04.5 in WSL2 with WSLg on a Windows 11 host, x86_64 (8 logical CPUs, 20 GB). Not tested: bare metal or a full VM boot, other distributions (the Ubuntu 22.04 and other targets of T059 have no record), other desktops and compositors, real GPU or software-rendering differences, Linux ARM or i686. Timings and memory are those of this WSL2 virtual machine; the first '--probe' run (cold start) was the slowest, 239 ms.

C++ RUNTIME: the current build links the distribution's libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1 dynamically (meson option static_cxx_runtime, default false, ADR 0004). The static variant (-Dstatic_cxx_runtime=true, about 296,952 bytes, asks for GLIBC_2.38) builds but was not run in this trial and was never tried on a system without a libstdc++.so.6 from GCC 5 or later. The loader's behaviour on a distribution older than Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc below 2.34) is not verified: the executable imports GLIBC_2.34.

MEMORY: peak_rss_kb is the application's own VmHWM; the cross-check with os.wait4 ru_maxrss of the child (136 to 496 kB higher, includes pre-exec pages) shows the same order of magnitude but is not an independent measurement of the same quantity. Memory was not measured with a long greeting or over a long session.

No procedure document exists yet for this trial (validation/procedures/linux.md is task T111), so the verdict carries no 'reproduction' path; the commands used are in the 'notes' field and the drivers (probe-series.py, gui-driver.py, glyphs-shoot.py, fake-uname.c) are in tools/trials/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/ of the main repository.
